title: The Lord rebukes the delay in building his house
setting: Joseph Smith dictated this revelation in Kirtland, Ohio, on 1 June 1833. Revelations in December 1832 and January 1833 had commanded a house of the Lord and a school. In May a conference named Hyrum Smith, Reynolds Cahoon, and Jared Carter to raise funds for it. Nearly a month later, no one had begun to build. A council then appointed Joseph Smith, Sidney Rigdon, and Frederick G. Williams to plan the inner court, and work began by 7 June.
summary: The revelation opens by saying the Lord chastens those he loves to prepare their deliverance. It rebukes them for a “very grievous sin”: neglecting the command to build the house meant to prepare his apostles. Many have been called, but few chosen, and those not chosen walk “in darkness at noon-day”. The voice says the chosen will be endowed with power from on high in this house. They must tarry, as the apostles did at Jerusalem. It also names contention in the school of the prophets as grievous. The house is to be built not after the world’s manner but by a pattern shown to three men. It will measure fifty-five by sixty-five feet, with a lower court for worship and a higher court for the apostles’ school.

contextNote.title: Why the house could not wait
contextNote.text: The Saints had the command but had not begun to build. Verse 3 calls the delay a “very grievous sin”. Verse 8 explains why it mattered: in this house the Lord would “endow” the chosen “with power from on high”. Verse 9 compares this to the apostles at Jerusalem, who were told to wait for promised power. Verse 11 adds the condition: keeping the commandments brings “power to build it”. In this passage, to endow means to give power to those being prepared for the ministry.

ldsText: The 2025 Come, Follow Me lesson for sections 94–97, “For the Salvation of Zion,” connects this revelation with the blessings promised in the Lord’s house. According to verses 1–2 and 8–9, what was the Lord offering the Saints through this rebuke?
reviewNote: Read all 17 verses. Official heading gives Kirtland, 1 June 1833, as a continuation of the directions to build the Lord’s house. JSP introduction read for the 4 May building committee, its 1 June circular, the delay, the planning committee of Smith, Rigdon, and Williams, and work begun by 7 June. Reynolds Cahoon and Jared Carter appear only in the setting; their ids are proposed in section 94 and not listed here. The JSP does not describe the school contentions of verse 10.
